literature_proposed.summary: Known, from a preprint: this node is the case L ≤ N of Yamada's Theorem 1.1. For N ≥ 500000 the bound N(1.3132 log²(2N) − 2.00271) is far above N, so the theorem rules out every collision in the node's range. The proof uses explicit prime-gap results, estimates for the largest prime factor of a product of consecutive integers, and an explicit Stirling formula. It has not been formalised, and the preprint has not been refereed as far as is known.
